correctness.rationale: The high-frequency decomposition u=a+v+z, first harmonic v and complement z, has exact d²=2(1−a), s=d²−d⁴/4, spectral high-mode energy excess Q(z)>=p||z||² with p=q_n or 1. For any candidate sequence with bounded Δ/d⁴, a cubic-deficit coercivity estimate completes the square to force Q(z)=O(d⁴), excluding hidden high-frequency competitors; then z=d²w. The second harmonic g=e²−1, ||g||²=1/2, eigen-excess p gives minimal limiting cubic term 1/4−1/(8p), and the entropy Taylor remainder gives +1/4, yielding 3/4−1/(4p). The explicit first-plus-second harmonic family attains equality. Independently evaluated normalized finite-cycle functions at n=5,6,9,13 for nearest-neighbor and word-length models with r=.002; observed ratios approach all eight predicted constants (maximum discrepancy about 1.7e−4), confirming normalization, not proving arbitrary-direction bound.
